question.worked_solution:
To solve this equation, we need both exponential terms to have a common base. To do this, we rewrite the equation using $16={2}^{4}$ and $8={2}^{3},$ as follows:

$$
{({2}^{4})}^{2n}={({2}^{3})}^{n+1}\,
$$

Then, we apply the power rule of exponents. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{8n} & ={2}^{3(n+1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since both sides of the equation share the same base $(2)$, we equate the exponents and solve for $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}8n & =3(n+1) \\ 8n & =3n+3 \\ 5n & =3 \\ n & =\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
